source_refs.note: Natural and induced mutations and the box on mutations in evolution (PDF 142-143).

items: Natural (spontaneous) mutations arise from sequencing errors or DNA damage during replication. They are part of the process of evolution and can be beneficial, neutral or harmful.

Induced mutations are caused by external factors: mutagenic substances or radiation, chemicals in the environment such as some pesticides and industrial pollutants, or medical treatments such as chemotherapy. They can have serious effects on health.

blocks.title: Mutations: contributors to evolution
blocks.text: The ultimate sources of all genetic variation are mutation and recombination. They create new DNA sequences (alleles) and new combinations of alleles, which form new traits that may be advantageous, harmful or neutral. Natural selection acts on these variations, the frequencies of alleles for advantageous traits increase, and in the long run this leads to evolution.

blocks.prompt: Give one example of a source of induced mutation.
blocks.explanation: Any one: radiation, mutagenic chemicals, certain pesticides or industrial pollutants, chemotherapy.

items: Natural mutations: replication errors or damage; part of evolution.
Induced mutations: radiation, chemicals, pollutants, chemotherapy.
Mutation and recombination supply variation for natural selection.
